proof_attempt_summary: The full-class minimax risk and honest-interval frontier were derived with quantitative cycle-deletion certificates and constrained transfer. The single authorized replacement removed the unavailable van der Vaart citation by a direct likelihood-ratio argument using checked Mathlib disintegration APIs; the resumed math and all five cited-source checks passed. The independent general-review score cap stopped the run below field, with related-work positioning unrepaired; formalization was not reached and no Lean proof module was produced.
tldr: For the specified four-treatment causal network, \(n\)-scaled minimax squared risk and \(\sqrt n\)-scaled \(90\%\)-honest connected-interval length have sharp Gaussian--Poisson limits. Explicit data-only randomized procedures attain both limits and have finite-sample coverage at least \(90\%\) for every sufficiently large \(n\); certified programs and approximating least-favorable support sequences characterize the constants. At \(q=0,c=1\), deleting \(BC\) or \(CD\) costs more than \(0.003632208133994\), and deleting \(AD\) costs more than \(0.009824867374614\), in limiting scaled squared risk. These comparisons cover the full legal polytope and the complete independently unknown intensity box. The equal-intensity scalar reduction remains a separate benchmark.
gap: Regular conditional-effect transport and optimal Gaussian confidence theory do not characterize an all-procedure honest frontier when several effect-modifier cells retain finite information. Archived mixed-experiment proposals leave count-using original-data attainment and explicit coverage ledgers unresolved.
fill: The focal objects are \(R_\star,L_\star\), their certified programs, and a two-sided constrained transfer with explicit error schedules. The strict cycle-versus-deletion comparison makes the finite-information network geometry substantive rather than decorative.
